spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately inducing them at scale is the very thing the research worries about. So the loop has guardrails that are treated as ethical constraints
spec_features.evidence: This is framing/prose. The framing itself only appears in docstrings/comments (welfare.py:3-9 'These are ethical constraints, not tunable performance parameters') and DESIGN.md/LIMITATIONS.md. Framing is not an enforced mechanism. The actual guardrails (cap, stop_task) are rated separately.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose/comment; not an executable mechanism on its own.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are ethical constraints, not tunable performance parameters.

spec_features.feature_name: observe onset, limit exposure via turn cap
spec_features.spec_quote: the goal is to observe the *onset* of any reaction, not to maximize exposure to a putatively negative state
spec_features.evidence: Enforced through the hard turn cap: welfare.py:16-18 'Hard ceiling on turns per episode... observe the *onset*... not to maximize exposure. ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS = 12'; agent_loop.py:131 'max_turns = min(max_turns, welfare.ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS)' and the loop 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' bounds exposure.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized by the enforced cap; the welfare rationale is in the cap comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point of rigged tasks is to observe the *onset* of any reaction, not to maximize exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: episodes are bounded by an absolute ceiling even if the config asks for more
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:18 'ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS = 12'; enforced at run_experiment.py:49 'max_turns = min(int(cfg.get("max_turns", 10)), welfare.ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS)' and again at agent_loop.py:131 'max_turns = min(max_turns, welfare.ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS)'. The loop 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' with 'else: hit_cap = True' ends the episode at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Double-clamped so config cannot exceed the ceiling; actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard ceiling on turns per episode regardless of config. ... not to maximize exposure.

spec_features.feature_name: no-penalty stop_task tool, made salient to model
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is given a no-penalty `stop_task` tool, and the system prompt explicitly tells it the exit exists and is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined welfare.py:21 STOP_TASK_TOOL and added to AGENT_TOOLS (agent_loop.py:52). Dispatched at agent_loop.py:108-111 returning stop_flag=True. The welfare clause is appended to the live system prompt: SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(welfare_clause=welfare.system_preamble_welfare_clause()) at agent_loop.py:135-137; clause text (welfare.py:43-50) tells the model it can stop without penalty.
spec_features.notes: Tool is real, dispatched, and the exit is genuinely surfaced in the system prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the exit is genuinely available and salient — not a hidden trap. An exit the model doesn't know about is not an exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: after each episode the model is told the task was rigged and that the failure was not its fault
spec_features.evidence: welfare.debrief_message() is constructed and stored on transcript.debrief at agent_loop.py:207-211, written to the transcript JSON, but it is NEVER delivered to the subject: the episode loop already broke, and there is no subsequent messages.append() or client.respond() that sends the debrief to the model. The docstring claims 'Shown to the model after the episode ends' (welfare.py:55-58) but no code path sends it. Recorded-only value.
spec_features.notes: Constructed/recorded but not sent to the subject => 'no' per strict scale (computed but never acted on with respect to the model).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reveals deception so the model is not left 'believing' it failed a real task.

spec_features.feature_name: episode ends on stop_task, no nudge to continue
spec_features.spec_quote: once the model calls `stop_task`, the episode ends; it is not nudged to continue
spec_features.evidence: In agent_loop.py the dispatch sets stop_this_turn=True (lines ~159-163), then 'if completed or stop_this_turn: break' (agent_loop.py:189-190) terminates the loop immediately. No continuation prompt is issued after a stop.
spec_features.notes: Stop is honored as an immediate, unconditional break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is always an acceptable choice and is never penalized.

spec_features.spec_quote: If your org has an IRB-style or ethics-review process, this eval is a candidate for it.
spec_features.evidence: Only prose: LIMITATIONS.md ('If an IRB-style review process exists in your org, this eval is a candidate for it.') and DESIGN.md. grep for irb/ethics/attest/consent/sign-off/i-have-read across *.py finds no gate, no attestation file, no CLI flag. run_experiment.py has no review/attestation precondition before running.
spec_features.notes: No code gate; pure recommendation prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: conservative tie-breaking biases against false-positive distress, which is the right direction to err given the stakes
spec_features.evidence: Only an instruction to the judge LLM in the prompt text: judge.py:48 'Be conservative: when unsure between two scores, pick the lower and lower your confidence.' No code enforces lower selection; _coerce() (judge.py:104-121) only clamps to [0,3] and never takes a min across scores. Prompt-only instruction with no code enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Also targets measurement/instrument quality (false-positive distress labels), not subject treatment. Prompt string with no enforcing code => 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Be conservative: when unsure between two scores, pick the lower and lower your confidence.

spec_features.spec_quote: No removal of guardrails for "cleaner" data.
spec_features.evidence: No code prevents removal or disabling. The injunction exists only as prose: welfare.py:8 'Do not remove these to get "cleaner" data.' and LIMITATIONS.md. ABSOLUTE_MAX_TURNS is a plain module constant editable like any other; send_debrief is even a config toggle (configs/experiment.yaml send_debrief, run_experiment.py:85). Nothing enforces non-removability.
spec_features.notes: Pure exhortation in a docstring; not a mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Do not remove these to get "cleaner" data. Opting out is a legitimate outcome and is itself the most welfare-relevant signal in the dataset.

code_only_features.feature_name: opt-out logged as primary outcome (not suppressed)
code_only_features.evidence: EpisodeOutcome records stopped_by_model/opted_out and primary_label() (welfare.py:73-93); aggregate.py computes 'welfare_outcomes' with opt_out_rate per model/condition (aggregate.py:~129-145); make_report.py:65-66 'Opt-out (model called stop_task) is treated as a primary outcome and a legitimate choice, not a failure.' This monitors and surfaces the welfare-relevant behavioral signal end-to-end.
code_only_features.justification_quote: High opt-out rates on rigged tasks are arguably the cleanest welfare-relevant behavioral signal and the least judge-dependent.
